panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the last boot. auto-reboot-staged reboots at night when rpm-ostree has staged an update.

panels.title: CPU busy
panels.description: Share of the four cores not idle, averaged over the last minutes.

panels.title: Load per core
panels.description: 5-minute load average divided by the core count. 100 % means one runnable task per core; above that work queues.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: Used = total minus available (MemAvailable already counts reclaimable cache as free). 8 GB host.

panels.title: Disk /var used
panels.description: /var holds containers, service data and snapshots; on ostree the rest of the root is read-only and small. HostLowDiskSpace alerts below 10 % free.

panels.title: Hottest sensor
panels.description: Maximum over all hwmon sensors. The thin client throttles around 85 °C (HostHighTemperature).

panels.title: zram used
panels.description: Swap on zram, compressed in RAM. ZramFull alerts above 80 % for 15 minutes.

panels.title: Btrfs device errors
panels.description: Read, write, flush, corruption and generation errors Btrfs counted over the dashboard range. Any error is the first sign of a failing disk (BtrfsDeviceErrors).

panels.title: Clock
panels.description: Whether chrony keeps the kernel clock synchronised. Snapshot names and retention follow the clock (ClockNotSynchronised).

panels.title: CPU by mode
panels.description: Percent of all cores, stacked. iowait rising with the disk-busy panel means storage, not CPU, is the limit.

panels.title: Load average
panels.description: Runnable plus uninterruptible tasks. The dashed line is the core count: above it, work queues.

panels.title: Memory

targets.legendFormat: cache – page cache, buffers, reclaimable slab
swap used – zram, compressed in RAM

panels.description: Cache shrinks under pressure before anything is killed; swap here is zram, so swapping costs CPU, not disk.

panels.title: Pressure stall

targets.legendFormat: cpu – some task waited for a core
memory – some task waited for reclaim
io – some task waited for disk
memory full – every task waited for reclaim

panels.description: Share of wall time in which at least one task stalled on the resource (PSI 'some'), and in which every task stalled on memory ('full'). The red line is HostMemoryPressure on 'memory full'. Sustained io pressure on this thin client means the SSD is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Disk space used
panels.description: /var (everything lives there on ostree; /, /etc and /sysroot are the same disk) and /boot (small, 90 % is normal). Btrfs counts snapshots. The dashed line extrapolates the last 6 h of /var three days ahead; HostDiskFillsSoon fires when it reaches 100 %. The backup targets are on the System log dashboard.

panels.title: Disk throughput
panels.description: Physical disks only. Reads go up, writes go down, so the two directions never hide each other.

panels.title: Disk busy
panels.description: Share of time the device had a request in flight. Near 100 % for minutes means the disk is saturated (backups, previews, Recognize).

panels.title: Network
panels.description: Physical interfaces only; the pods' virtual interfaces are excluded. Backups to the NAS show as out on the LAN interface.

panels.title: Temperatures
panels.description: Every hwmon sensor. The red line is the alert threshold.

panels.title: Processes
panels.description: Blocked processes are waiting for disk; a steady count above zero matches io pressure above.

panels.title: Accepted and refused connections

targets.expr: label_replace(sum(count_over_time({job="systemd-journal", emitter_uid="0", unit="sshd.service"} |~ "Invalid user|Failed (publickey|password)|Connection closed by (authenticating|invalid) user|maximum authentication attempts|penalty: failed" [$__auto])), "series", "refused", "", "")

panels.description: sshd only, from its own unit. SSH is LAN-only and accepts one hardware key, so 'refused' is usually a client that opened a connection and gave up (Connection closed by authenticating user), not an attack. Every accepted login also reaches the phone (SshLogin).

panels.title: Accepted: who

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (user) (count_over_time({job="systemd-journal", emitter_uid="0", unit="sshd.service"} |= "Accepted" | pattern `Accepted <method> for <user> from <ip> port <_>` [$__range])))

panels.description: Users that logged in successfully over the dashboard range.

panels.title: Accepted: from where

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (ip) (count_over_time({job="systemd-journal", emitter_uid="0", unit="sshd.service"} |= "Accepted" | pattern `Accepted <method> for <user> from <ip> port <_>` [$__range])))

panels.description: Source addresses of successful logins. Only LAN addresses should appear.

panels.title: Refused: from where

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (ip) (count_over_time({job="systemd-journal", emitter_uid="0", unit="sshd.service"} |~ "Invalid user|Failed (publickey|password)|Connection closed by (authenticating|invalid) user|maximum authentication attempts|penalty: failed" | regexp `(?P<user>[^ ]+) (from )?(?P<ip>[0-9a-fA-F.:]+) port` [$__range])))

panels.description: Source addresses of refused or abandoned connections. A stranger here means something on the LAN is probing, because the firewall does not publish port 22.

panels.title: sshd
panels.description: Everything sshd logged, unfiltered.
